clue.text: That's my view (to the extent that 13 may allow)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a phrase offering one's personal opinion

definitions.text: to the extent that 13 may allow
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally, as far as short-sighted eyes can make things out, 13 being MYOPIA

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket points to 13 across, short-sightedness, so the second sense is a literal limit on how far one can see.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for giving an opinion, and also literally describes the limit of a person's eyesight.

clue.text: When soaring, grouse endlessly seen in island group

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means the word goes upward, so it is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to grouse is to moan or complain

explanation.surface: A complaining game bird glimpsed while flying over a Pacific archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: Grouse looks like the bird but is the verb, to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is a chain of Pacific islands, so it is an archipelago or island group.

clue.text: Certainly no motorway out of the country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., a minor road that is certainly not a motorway
second meaning: overseas, in a foreign land

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain roads are graded M (motorway), A and B; a B road is a lesser route, so split the answer as A B-ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being overseas, in a foreign land rather than at home.

clue.text: Conspirator managed with church rather than lean-to

indicators.note: rather than means one word is put in the place of the other

parts.note: to have managed something is to have accomplished it
a lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A plotter got things done by meeting in a church instead of a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is a partner in crime, someone who plots or conspires with another.

clue.text: Could this be stormy Lewis wife departs?

definitions.text: Could this be stormy Lewis wife departs?

indicators.note: stormy means the remaining letters are thrown about into a new order
departs means the letter for wife leaves the name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wondering question about a windswept Hebridean island once one's wife has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis is an island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is a Hebridean island, and an isle is any island, so the result names what Lewis is.

clue.text: Daily battle with army: enemy tank occasionally damaged? Nonsense

indicators.note: damaged means all these letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report on a regular fight in which the enemy's tank is now and then hit.
explanation.walkthrough: All my eye and Betty Martin is an old British expression dismissing something as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned idiom for rubbish or claptrap, said of something one does not believe.

clue.text: Groveller quiet about Yard PC seen with soldier?

indicators.note: about means the quiet sound wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
a PC is a police constable, a cop
an ant is a soldier in crossword terms, after the soldier ant

explanation.surface: A toady keeps quiet about a Scotland Yard constable working with a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: Yard suggests Scotland Yard, but here it simply gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant is a flatterer or toady, someone who grovels to win favour.

clue.text: Gay insults here recollected in talk about London?

indicators.note: recollected, read as re-collected, means the letters are gathered again in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remembered abuse turns up in a discussion of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is the accent of London and the Thames estuary; the question mark flags that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary English is a way of speaking associated with London and the surrounding Thames area, so it is talk of that region.

clue.text: See 6
Union woman at first liked using arithmetic values

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
Erica is a woman's name

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A union member enjoyed working with sums from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerical describes anything expressed in or relating to numbers.

clue.text: Legal officer briefly touring here in Paris

indicators.note: touring means the officer goes round the next piece

parts.note: LT is the short form of lieutenant
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A legal officer, in short, is visiting Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit is a formal word for lawful or permitted.

clue.text: Perhaps grizzly members are equipped to fight

parts.note: a grizzly is one kind of bear
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Bears' limbs are apparently built for combat.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear arms is to carry weapons, so those who do are armed and ready to fight.

clue.text: Sigh providing clue for this looker's problem?

definitions.text: Sigh providing clue for this looker's problem?

parts.note: sigh is the word sight cut short, so it hints at short sight
a looker here is simply someone looking, whose eyesight is at fault

explanation.walkthrough: Sigh is sight with its last letter missing: short sight, the condition in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the medical name for short-sightedness, a defect of vision.

clue.text: Accordingly desires to accept censure, being bad loser?

definitions.note: the answer names the attitude of a bad loser rather than the person

parts.note: so can mean accordingly, as in 'and so'

indicators.note: to accept means the desires take the censure inside them

parts.note: urges are desires
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: So wanting to take the blame, being a poor sport?
explanation.walkthrough: Sour grapes, from Aesop's fox, is the resentful dismissal of something one failed to get.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour grapes is the bitter, belittling attitude typical of someone who cannot accept defeat gracefully.

clue.text: Value in warmth and love coming to African location

parts.note: a tog is a unit measuring the warmth of a duvet

explanation.surface: Finding warmth and affection on arriving in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Tog ratings are how British duvets are graded for warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Cheerfully roam, dashing to trap one skein of geese?

indicators.note: to trap means the dashing word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: dashing means gallant, debonair
geese fly in a V-shaped skein

explanation.surface: Flitting happily about, racing to catch a single flight of geese.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to go around enjoying oneself, wandering in search of fun.

clue.text: Red Queen supplies drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Mary I of England, nicknamed for the Protestants she had burned, a queen with blood on her hands
second meaning: a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice

explanation.walkthrough: Supplies is a link here; the queen's nickname and the cocktail share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Mary Tudor, the bloodstained queen, and to a vodka-and-tomato cocktail.

clue.text: Son in punt with sailor, leader of some magnitude

parts.note: a punt is pushed along with a long pole, which the clue lets stand for it
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A boy afloat in a punt with a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: The son goes after the punting pole; magnitude is the measure of a star's brightness, and the pole star leads navigators north.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, is a bright star that guides travellers, a leader in the sky.

clue.text: Booking sensational comedian

parts.note: yellow journalism is sensational reporting
a card is a joker, an amusing person

explanation.surface: A hotel reservation for a sensational comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Booking means being cautioned by the referee in football, not reserving a room.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a booking is a caution, shown by the referee holding up a yellow card.

clue.text: Reveal where learner truant in school?

indicators.note: a truant is absent, so the learner is missing from the phrase

parts.note: to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Disclosing where a pupil skipping classes might be found at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Kane's inspiration picks up payment at last

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's muse gets the money in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Kane is Charles Foster Kane of the film Citizen Kane, modelled on press baron William Randolph Hearst.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper magnate Hearst is widely seen as the model for Orson Welles's Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Constellation circling south comes into view

indicators.note: circling means the constellation surrounds the compass letter

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation

explanation.surface: A star group swinging round to the south appears in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to emerge or appear, coming into sight.

clue.text: Unstoppable decline in public brawl — men thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out means the men are ejected from the brawl

parts.note: a free-for-all is an open brawl anyone can join
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A street fight goes downhill once some men are ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: A free fall is a sudden, uncontrolled drop, as of prices or fortunes.

clue.text: Violence in the past involving King George

indicators.note: involving means the past word wraps round the king

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Bloodshed long ago in which King George played a part.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble, short for aggravation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British slang for aggressive behaviour or fighting.

clue.text: Signal to stop bombardment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a taxi is to wave it down
second meaning: a ... of bullets is a heavy barrage

explanation.walkthrough: One short word serves both as calling a vehicle over and as a barrage of missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail is a call to halt a cab or ship, and also a shower of missiles or questions.

clue.text: Arsenic found in rum? Bottoms up!

indicators.note: found in means the poison is placed inside the drink

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of rum

explanation.surface: A poisoner's drink, with a cheery cheers as it goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a drinking salute, the same as proposing a toast.

clue.text: Shoots soldier with sawn-off gun in lawless SAS

indicators.note: in places the soldier and short gun inside the regiment's letters
lawless means the regiment's letters run wild out of order

parts.note: taken as written
a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: sawn-off means the end of the weapon is cut away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A paratrooper fires a shotgun among rogue special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoots looks like a verb of gunfire but is a noun for young plant stems; the SAS is the British Special Air Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is eaten as tender young spears, the plant's edible shoots.

clue.text: Nationalist nuts letting in posh artist, allowing citizenship

definitions.note: the gerund names the act, matching the noun answer

indicators.note: letting in means the jumbled word admits the next pieces
nuts means the word is crazily rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
U means upper-class
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Mad patriots admit a classy painter, granting him a passport.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturalisation is the legal process by which a foreigner is granted the rights of a citizen.
